paper: Not All Information Is Worth Asking For: Decision-Informed Information Seeking with LLMs
setting: LLM decision-making with costly checks across 4 domains (controlled synthetic, UCI tabular, SEC filings); 20 LLMs; training-free
input_modality: Text only: numeric elicitation questions and textual evidence; no images, no physical environment
hidden_state: Unknown factual value / probability of a bad outcome; check reliability given in synthetic settings, estimated in real settings
budget: Per-check cost and explicit stopping rule; no physical step or task-time budget
planning_role: Elicits a small decision model (bad-outcome probability and how each check shifts it), values checks by imagined decision improvement net of cost; DIVA-U averages over uncertain strengths; DIVA-DP does exact DP over remaining acquisitions
oracle_privileges: Controlled environments state check reliabilities and provide an exact DP optimum as reference; real-data settings do not expose ground truth to the method
metrics: Regret relative to best possible decision; stopping behavior; cuts regret of best LLM baseline by 75 percent in synthetic scenarios
strongest_baseline: Direct, CoT, self-consistency, ReAct, Ask-P, VoI-P, VoI-Ask, BED-LLM, PAL (per official README)
remaining_gap: No visual observation, no environment control, no physical time cost, no latent dynamics that switch mid-episode; checks do not change future control options
contrast_with_ruleshift: RuleShift probes consume primitive steps in a physical loop and their value is in changing later actions under a law that may shift; requires a DIVA-style adapted physical-cost baseline
threat_to_novelty: HIGH - directly claims decision-informed value of information; must not claim first in VoI
verification_source: arXiv abstract page + official GitHub README fetched and checked

paper: Playing ZendoWorld: Challenging AI Agents on Active Visual Concept Induction
setting: Interactive visual rule induction: agents infer a hidden logical rule about visual scenes, propose new scenes to acquire evidence, and refine hypotheses from game feedback; includes human data
input_modality: Rendered visual game scenes plus symbolic/natural-language representations; Blender-rendered images and game feedback
hidden_state: Hidden logical rule of a Zendo game; induction target, not a control-relevant transition law
budget: Interaction budget for proposing scenes and receiving feedback; not a physical task-time or control-return budget
planning_role: Active experiment design to reduce hypothesis uncertainty; compared agents include VLM reasoning, Bayesian particle filtering, dynamic concept discovery, neuro-symbolic methods
oracle_privileges: Game master holds the true rule; human participant data collected for comparison
metrics: Rule-label prediction accuracy, true-rule recovery, expected information gain of proposed experiments, human-agent gap
strongest_baseline: Pure VLM reasoning, Bayesian particle filtering, dynamic concept discovery, neuro-symbolic agents
remaining_gap: Measures rule recovery and information acquisition rather than task return under shifting dynamics; proposed scenes are not physical probes with travel/test cost; no within-episode dynamics change
contrast_with_ruleshift: RuleShift measures closed-loop task return and value-aware physical probing when the active law can change after commitment; contrast return under shifting dynamics against rule recovery
threat_to_novelty: MEDIUM-HIGH - visual hypothesis induction and active experiments overlap strongly
verification_source: arXiv abstract page + official GitHub README fetched and checked

paper: EVOLvE: Evaluating and Optimizing LLMs For In-Context Exploration
setting: Benchmarks LLM exploration in contextual and context-free bandits with varying difficulty; measures and improves in-context decision-making under uncertainty
input_modality: Text/numeric bandit contexts and scalar reward feedback; no images
hidden_state: Unknown reward distributions of bandit arms; stateless exploration problem
budget: Interaction count / cumulative regret over the bandit session
planning_role: Algorithm-guided inference support and algorithm distillation via in-context demonstrations and fine-tuning on synthetic algorithm-generated data
oracle_privileges: Optimal exploration algorithms are supplied as inference support or distillation targets; this is a method input, not a hidden oracle used at evaluation
metrics: Cumulative regret, exploration efficiency, ablations on task difficulty and data representation; links exploration to model size
strongest_baseline: Larger LLMs without algorithmic guidance; algorithm-guided variants are the proposed improvement
remaining_gap: Stateless bandits: no visual observation, no hidden state, no probe action with physical cost, no within-episode change of transition law
contrast_with_ruleshift: RuleShift is a partially observable sequential control task with a physical probe/act trade-off and a hidden law that can switch mid-episode; regret is secondary to closed-loop return
threat_to_novelty: MEDIUM - exploration and regret prior art
verification_source: PMLR proceedings page fetched and checked (authors, volume, pages, year)

paper: Doing Experiments and Revising Rules with Natural Language and Probabilistic Reasoning
setting: Model of inferring natural-language rules by doing experiments; integrates LLMs with Monte Carlo probabilistic inference, interleaving online belief updates with information-theoretic experiment design; human-model comparison on a Zendo-style task
input_modality: Natural-language hypotheses and experiment feedback; no visual observations in the abstract
hidden_state: True rule, including fuzzy/probabilistic rules assumed necessary to fit human data
budget: Experiment design under information-theoretic criteria; no physical step or task-return budget
planning_role: Online Bayesian-style belief updates plus experiment design; compares with LLM hypothesis generation/revision algorithms
oracle_privileges: Ground-truth rule held by task; human data used for comparison (abstract does not describe an agent-facing oracle)
metrics: Rule-recovery accuracy, quality of experiment design, fit to human data
strongest_baseline: Recent algorithms for LLM-based hypothesis generation and revision (abstract does not name them)
remaining_gap: No visual perception, no physical control loop, no probe cost in the same reward stream, no mid-episode dynamics shift
contrast_with_ruleshift: RuleShift targets value-aware physical probing and closed-loop return when the governing law changes after interaction; this paper targets rule recovery and experiment design quality
threat_to_novelty: MEDIUM - language hypothesis updating and experiment design prior art
verification_source: NeurIPS proceedings abstract page fetched and checked (title, authors, venue, year)

paper: One Life to Learn: Inferring Symbolic World Models for Stochastic Environments from Unguided Exploration
setting: Learns symbolic world models in a complex stochastic environment (Crafter-OO reimplementation) under a limited interaction budget, with one life and no external task-specific guidance; uses conditionally activated programmatic laws in a probabilistic programming framework
input_modality: Structured object-oriented symbolic state and a pure transition function; explicitly NOT a raw RGB VLM setting
hidden_state: Stochastic transition laws expressed as precondition-effect programmatic laws
budget: Severe limited interaction budget; evaluation measures state ranking and state fidelity, plus planning utility
planning_role: Probabilistic-programming world-model learning with dynamic computation graph; planning via rollouts inside the learned model
oracle_privileges: Environment exposes a structured symbolic state and pure transition function to the learner; this is an environment API, not a privileged evaluator belief or Q-value
metrics: State ranking, state fidelity, planning utility in multi-step tasks; outperforms a strong baseline on 16 of 23 scenarios
strongest_baseline: A strong baseline not named in the abstract; full text not read
remaining_gap: Learns laws from scratch from symbolic state rather than choosing among public candidate descriptions; no visual VLM input, no physical probe cost, no within-episode law switch
contrast_with_ruleshift: RuleShift assumes known candidate mechanic descriptions and asks whether a frozen VLM pays a physical cost to disambiguate a law that can change mid-episode; world-model learning is complementary, not the same claim
threat_to_novelty: MEDIUM - symbolic world-model learning under limited interaction
verification_source: ICLR proceedings abstract page fetched and checked (title, authors, venue, year)
